chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I was with him when Nafi', the slave of Ibn Umar, passed by. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Are you the one who alleges that Ibn Umar divorced his wife once while she was menstruating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered Umar to instruct him to return to her?' He said, 'Yes.'

He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You lie, by Allah, the One there is no god except Him, regarding Ibn Umar. I heard Ibn Umar saying: I divorced her in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) three times, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) returned it to me, and I kept her after the divorce. Therefore, fear Allah, O Nafi', and do not narrate falsehood about Ibn Umar!'
ai.seo_question: What was the actual nature of Umar ibn al-Khattab's divorce during the Prophet's lifetime according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential stance on the validity of the triple divorce (ṭalāq al-thalāth) during the Prophet's lifetime, contrasting it with the Sunni view that it was initially one divorce made effective as three. Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) corrects the historical record by asserting that Umar divorced his wife three times and the Prophet accepted this, thereby validating the practice of three divorces in a single sitting even before the revelation of Quran 2:228 explicitly codified the waiting period (ʿiddah) rules. This incident serves as a key evidence for Shia scholars regarding the continuity of prophetic practice and the interpretation of early Islamic legal developments.
